articles.title: Brazil fines TikTok $30 mn in 'powerful signal' over child safety
articles.summary: Brazil's data protection agency on Tuesday fined TikTok nearly $30 million for failing to implement child safety measures in what it said was a "powerful sig...
articles.body:
Brazil's data protection agency on Tuesday fined TikTok nearly $30 million for failing to implement child safety measures in what it said was a "powerful signal" to social media companies.

Brazil has taken a tough stance on the regulation of social media platforms, cracking down on disinformation and requiring users under 16 to have their accounts linked to those of their parents.

Fabricio Lopes, an enforcement director with the ANPD data protection agency, told a press conference that TikTok "was not taking the necessary measures to prevent adolescents from accessing the platform and from having the data of these children and adolescents processed."

This data was "being used to offer advertising to adolescents."

He said the fine of 153.7 million reais ($29.9 million) was a "powerful signal to other platforms regarding how seriously the ANPD takes this work" and that the agency hoped they would "get the message."

TikTok agreed last week to pay $400 million to settle a lawsuit with the US Department of Justice over claims that the video-sharing platform collected children's personal data without parental permission.

The ANPD this month also ordered popular streaming platform Discord to suspend livestreams and video calls after a teenage girl was allegedly encouraged to take her own life during a broadcast.

The agency told AFP that an appeal filed by Discord on Monday against the suspension is under review.

ANPD director Lorena Giuberti Coutinho said the agency had last week initiated proceedings to verify the compliance of 22 social media networks and platforms with a law passed this year to protect children and teens online.

"I think we can expect much stronger enforcement action" in coming months, she said.

In addition to the fine, the ANPD ordered TikTok parent company ByteDance to delete data collected in violation of regulations.

Coutinho said TikTok had committed to suspending all advertisements for users who are not logged in.

TikTok has committed to "implementing a compliance plan to improve the protection of children and adolescents," the ANPD said.

The platform will be required to automatically apply stricter privacy settings to accounts belonging to children under the age of 16, strengthen parental supervision systems, and implement stricter content filters.

In a statement sent to AFP, TikTok said the fine stems from concerns raised in 2021 and "does not take into account" measures that have been implemented since then.

The statement said TikTok has rolled out over 50 safety features aimed at teens over the past six years.

These include restricting direct messaging for children under 16, not recommending this age group's content to strangers, and allowing parents to set screen-time limits and block accounts.

According to the ANPD, TikTok has ten days to appeal the fine.

In 2024, the platform X was blocked for 40 days in Brazil until the social media network owned by the world's richest person, Elon Musk, complied with the Supreme Court's orders to remove accounts spreading disinformation.

articles.title: Thousands of dragonflies are suddenly swarming across California, and the insects could help farmers control crop pests naturally
articles.summary: US News: California is seeing an unusual surge in dragonflies, with large groups appearing over parks, ponds and farms after warm spring and early summer rain..
articles.body: California is seeing an unusual surge in dragonflies, with large groups appearing over parks, ponds and farms after warm spring and early summer rain. The insects have been especially noticeable around the San Francisco Bay Area, where residents have reported seeing dozens flying together. Oakland nursery owner Peter Veilleux even counted about 100 dragonflies in one group while walking his dog near Lake Merritt. The sudden appearance may look mysterious, but experts say weather conditions probably created the right opportunity for the insects to spread. According to The Associated Press(AP), dragonfly expert Kathy Biggs believes warm monsoon storms helped drive the increase, with many of the insects likely being âwandering gliders,â a migratory species capable of travelling long distances. For Californians, the spectacle is not only striking but also useful, because these natural predators feed on mosquitoes and crop pests.Warm spring rains triggering huge dragonfly swarmsKathy Biggs, a dragonfly expert and co-author of âDragonflies of California,â told AP that unusually warm monsoon storms moved through the state during late spring and early summer. Those conditions appear to have helped produce the huge number now being seen. Many of the dragonflies are probably wandering gliders. Unlike species that remain close to the water where they emerge, wandering gliders are highly migratory and can turn up in large numbers when weather conditions are favourable. The insects can travel long distances by taking advantage of changes in air pressure. Biggs described their movement as effectively âsurfingâ the pressure systems created by the monsoon weather. They can reach speeds of about 35 mph (56 kph), allowing them to cover considerable distances. That explains why people in different parts of California can suddenly encounter large swarms of dragonflies. The insects do not necessarily remain in one location for long. Biggs said migratory species can stay somewhere for only a few days before moving on.What dragonflies are doing around farms in CaliforniaThe swarms are more than an unusual summer sight. They are also providing farmers with a natural form of pest control. AP reported that Joe Del Bosque, who farms in Fresno County noticed unusually large numbers of dragonflies flying about 10 to 20 feet (3 to 6 metres) above him earlier in August. Dragonflies are welcome visitors on his farm because they prey on insects that can damage crops. Del Bosque said the dragonflies feed on aphids, whiteflies and fruit flies, while also catching larger flying insects such as adult aphids and moths. He compared the insects to tiny fighter jets because of the way they rapidly chase and capture prey in mid-air. Ladybirds also help control pests around the crops, but dragonflies bring a different advantage by targeting insects while they are flying.Why are dragonflies such effective huntersDragonflies are remarkably efficient predators. Chris Grinter, senior collection manager of entomology at the California Academy of Sciences in San Francisco, said that their strong flight muscles, excellent vision and agility make them particularly effective hunters. More than 90% of their hunting attempts are successful. He also said a dragonfly can eat hundreds of mosquitoes in a single day. That makes the sudden California swarms potentially beneficial for people as well as farms. California has about 70 species of dragonflies, although most are not migratory. Many remain close to the places where they emerge. The wandering gliders responsible for much of the current spectacle are different because they can travel with changing weather systems.Life cycle of dragonfliesThe swarms seen above California are only the brief flying stage of a much longer life cycle. Dragonflies spend most of their lives underwater. After mating, females lay tiny eggs in freshwater. Once the eggs hatch, the young insects, known as nymphs, remain underwater and hunt other small creatures. According to AP, this underwater stage can last at least six months and, for some species, as long as five years. During that time, nymphs can feed on mosquito larvae, tadpoles and even other dragonfly nymphs. Eventually, they emerge from the water, shed their skin and become the familiar four-winged insects seen around ponds and fields. Their wings can move independently, allowing them to fly forwards, backwards, upwards and downwards and even hover in place. Once airborne, however, their lives are relatively short. Adults may survive for only a few weeks or months, spending that time hunting, moving between freshwater habitats and reproducing.People who enjoy watching dragonflies can make their gardens more welcoming to them. Biggs recommends avoiding pesticides and creating fish-free ponds where dragonflies can reproduce. Sunny areas with places for the insects to perch can also provide suitable conditions. Such spaces can offer dragonflies somewhere to rest while giving them access to the small insects they hunt. The sight nevertheless offers a reminder of how quickly insects can respond when weather, water and food come together.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: West African cyber-crime networks: Mass arrests follow Interpol crackdown
articles.summary: The operation included the arrest of 39 people in South Africa for romance and investment scams.
articles.body:
Fifty-eight people linked to organised West African cyber-crime groups have been arrested in an operation across 22 countries and six continents.

Dubbed "Operation Jackal IV", it was co-ordinated by the global policing agency Interpol, targeting those behind romance and investment scams. It also identified 263 suspects.

Interpol said it was a response to the escalating global threat posed by these criminal networks - such as the feared Nigerian Black Axe group - believed to be behind a "significant share" of cyber-enabled financial fraud.

The operation also allowed analysis of emerging trends such as how these groups use sextortion to target minors, with victims as young as 14.

The ultra-violent cult that became a global mafia Published 13 December 2021

The ultra-violent cult that became a global mafia

Operation Jackal IV - which took place between November 2025 and June 2026 - investigated how the groups laundered money and how financial fraud cyber crimes, such as cryptocurrency and email compromise fraud, were conducted.

Scams often targeted "retirees in English-speaking countries", Interpol said.

"By following illicit financial flows across borders, we are attacking the very lifeblood of organised crime and making it increasingly difficult for criminal networks to profit from their activities," Tomonobu Kaya, director of Interpol's financial crime centre, said in a statement.

"Operation Jackal IV demonstrates the power of international co-operation."

During the operation, Interpol helped with cross-border co-ordination and intelligence sharing.

It also provided support and specialised training for money-laundering investigations with the participating countries.

Interpol said many aspects of Jackal IV remained under investigation but preliminary outcomes included arrests in Argentina, Italy, Romania and South Africa.

In South Africa, seven sites linked to a syndicate involved in romance and investment scams were raided.

The policing agency was on scene in Johannesburg to support local authorities during the raids.

South African police made 39 arrests, seized $2.67m (£1.96m) and blocked 257 bank accounts.

As well as cyber-enabled fraud, the West African networks also participated in other serious and violent crimes, Interpol said.

Operation Jackal IV is one of multiple "Jackal" police operations that have taken place since 2022.

In 2024, Jackal III led to the arrests of 300 people linked to Black Axe and other affiliated groups.

Black Axe is a shadowy criminal network with trafficking, prostitution and killing operations around the world.

Nigeria is its main recruitment ground and many of its members are university educated and inducted during their schooling.

articles.title: Kurdish-led SDF announces dissolution, integration into Syrian state
articles.summary: The commander of the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) Mazloum Abdi announced the dissolution of the group on Tuesday, saying it would be fully inte...
articles.body:
The commander of the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) Mazloum Abdi announced the dissolution of the group on Tuesday, saying it would be fully integrated into Syrian state institutions.

In a press statement delivered at the presidential palace in Damascus after a meeting with transitional President Ahmad al-Sharaa, Abdi said the Kurdish Autonomous Administration in north-eastern Syria - established during the country's civil war - would also be dissolved.

Abdi said the SDF's mission had ended and that the group was moving "from the phase of defence to the phase of building Syria."

Abdi said that "all military and civilian formations" affiliated with the SDF and the Kurdish Autonomous Administration would also be integrated into state institutions.

The SDF was formally established in October 2015 and became the main US-backed force fighting Islamic State in north-eastern Syria.

The announcement represents a major step toward ending the separate military and administrative structures that Kurdish-led authorities have maintained in parts of north-eastern Syria since the fall of long-time dictator Bashar al-Assad in late 2024.

Under Assad, Kurds were marginalized and faced restrictions on cultural and linguistic expression, while a 1962 census left tens of thousands without Syrian citizenship.

After government forces withdrew from large parts of north-eastern Syria during the 2011 uprising, Kurdish forces established control over much of the area.

Following the fall of al-Assad in December 2024, Damascus and the Kurdish-led authorities began negotiations over the future of the SDF and the administration of north-eastern Syria.

articles.title: In 1903, rabbits were released on Hawaiiâs Laysan Island as a food source; within a decade they had nearly stripped it bare, and three of its five landbird species eventually went extinct
articles.summary: US News: When German immigrant Max Schlemmer brought a small number of domestic rabbits to the isolated Pacific atoll of Laysan in 1903, he hoped to create a p.
articles.body: When German immigrant Max Schlemmer brought a small number of domestic rabbits to the isolated Pacific atoll of Laysan in 1903, he hoped to create a profitable meat-canning business. He also saw the animals as a source of entertainment for his children while he worked on guano extraction operations. Instead, the decision caused one of the worst ecological disasters in modern conservation history. Within a decade, the rabbits had stripped much of the island of its vegetation and eventually helped drive three of its five unique landbird species to extinction. Historical records preserved by the PapahÄnaumokuÄkea Marine National Monument show how quickly the rabbit population grew across the isolated 1,000-acre atoll. With no natural predators and an enormous appetite, the rabbits consumed vegetation faster than the island could replace it. Over the next 20 years, the uncontrolled population destroyed 26 native plant species, including the unique Laysan fan palm (Pritchardia) and native sandalwood trees (Santalum ellipticum). A once-green habitat for birds was gradually turned into a landscape of bare sand.Devastating losses among native birdsThe destruction of the island's vegetation had a severe effect on its native birds. Before non-native mammals arrived, Laysan supported huge seabird colonies and five species of landbirds that existed nowhere else in the world. As shrubs, tussock grass and trees disappeared, so did insects and places where birds could shelter and nest. The loss of vegetation contributed to the extinction of three endemic birds: the Laysan millerbird (Acrocephalus familiaris familiaris), Laysan rail (Zapornia palmeri) and Laysan honeycreeper (Himatione fraithii). Scientific records from the 1923 Tanager Expedition documented the final days of the Laysan honeycreeper. The expedition was organised by the US Department of Agriculture's Bureau of Biological Survey and the Bernice P. Bishop Museum. Ornithologist Alexander Wetmore recorded that the last three Laysan honeycreepers died during a severe sandstorm while scientists were on the island trying to remove the remaining rabbits. The small, flightless Laysan rail survived for a time on nearby Midway Atoll after birds were introduced there in 1891. However, that population was later wiped out during World War II after rats were accidentally introduced to the atoll. This resulted in the complete extinction of the species.Narrow escape for surviving speciesOnly two of Laysan's endemic landbirds survived the crisis: the Laysan finch (Telespiza cantans) and the critically endangered Laysan duck (Anas laysanensis). Both species survived partly by changing what they ate. They began feeding on carrion, abandoned seabird eggs and brine flies around the island's central hypersaline lagoon. According to a historical overview and restoration plan from the US Fish and Wildlife Service, the Laysan duck population fell to dangerously low levels during the habitat destruction. By the early 20th century, fewer than 20 birds were believed to remain in the world. As the damage spread across the Northwestern Hawaiian Archipelago, President Theodore Roosevelt took action. In 1909, he issued an executive order creating the Hawaiian Islands Bird Reservation. Federal authorities later removed Schlemmer from Laysan following indictments linked to illegal feather collection and the unauthorised introduction of invasive species.Eradication and recoveryBy 1918, the rabbits had consumed much of their own food supply. Only a few hundred starving animals remained on an island with badly damaged vegetation. The crisis finally ended in 1923, when the Tanager Expedition arrived on Laysan with armed field crews tasked with finding and killing the remaining rabbits. After the rabbits were completely removed, the US Fish and Wildlife Service began long-term habitat restoration work. Conservation efforts continue today under the PapahÄnaumokuÄkea Marine National Monument. Over the following decades, native bunchgrass (Eragrostis variabilis) and coastal shrubs slowly returned. Their growth helped stabilise the soil and reduce the sandstorms that had threatened the island's central lagoon. Conservationists have also reintroduced related plant species and created protected populations of the surviving Laysan duck and Laysan finch on other protected atolls, including Midway and Eastern Island. To help replace an extinct bird, federal wildlife managers also moved the closely related Nihoa millerbird (Acrocephalus familiaris kingi) from Nihoa Island to Laysan in 2011. The new population became established successfully, marking an important step in rebuilding an island ecosystem that had been severely damaged by a small group of domestic rabbits introduced more than a century earlier.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Foreign students must make an official request for authorization: ICE issues new memo as colleges pause CPT program; American students will also have to complete training
articles.summary: US News: As US universities started pausing CPT (Curricular Practical Training), which is a temporary work authorization for F-1 students, triggering confusion.
articles.body: As US universities started pausing CPT (Curricular Practical Training), which is a temporary work authorization for F-1 students, triggering confusion over the future of international students in the US, Immigration and Customs Enforcement issued another memo clarifying and doubling down on the new restrictions. CPT allows F-1 students to gain off-campus work experience, internships, before graduating and hence it has to be related to the student's major. For approval of these internships, students do not have to go to immigration; the university itself can approve them. ICE said the university administration is not giving these approvals judiciously.On August 12, ICE issued a directive to all schools and universities stating that CPT has to be an integral part of the course. Many universities, including UC Berkeley, UC Davis, UC San Diego, Purdue, Santa Clara paused the approvals of CPT programs.In the new memo, ICE explained some of the frequently asked questions and made it clear that all students attending the same course must do CPT as it must be mandatory. American students, too, will have to do this, otherwise it's not valid because it's not mandatory then.How is CPT defined in regulation?A foreign student may be authorized by a DSO (Designated School Official) to participate in a CPT program that is an integral part of an established curriculum. Curricular practical training is defined as alternative work/study, internship, cooperative education or any other type of required internship or practicum that is offered by sponsoring employers through cooperative agreements with the school.How is CPT different from Optional Practical Training?Optional Practical Training (OPT) is training that is not an integral part of a studentâs established curriculum. OPT is not intended to fulfill the requirements of a studentâs program of study and successful program completion does not require participation in OPT; it is optional. In contrast, CPT fulfills an integral element of an established curriculum and successful completion is contingent on participation in CPT.Can CPT be offered as a part of an elective course?In any instance where an elective course is optional, making the CPT optional, the integral and required aspects of CPT would not be met. CPT is an integral part of an established curriculum and the practical training is required for all students participating in that curriculum, regardless of citizenship.Because CPT is allowed only where the training is an integral part of an established curriculum, does that mean that all students enrolled in the established curriculum must participate in and complete practical training?Yes. Unlike OPT, participation in CPT is not optional for any student participating in an established curriculum that the school has determined requires CPT as an integral part of the educational experience. This means that all students â foreign and American â are required to participate in practical training if they are enrolled in an established curriculum where practical training is integral.The question-answer part of the memo said that while auditing and investigating schools to ensure compliance, SEVP (Student and Exchange Visitor Program) has noted that some institutions have described CPT as if it is optional practical training and not integral, despite clear regulatory requirements. SEVP has also discovered that some institutions have not required all students enrolled in the same established curriculum to participate in practical training, despite clear regulatory requirements that CPT is permitted only where the practical training is an integral part of an established curriculum.Are foreign students required to proactively request CPT authorization from their DSO?Yes. Foreign students must make an official request for authorization for CPT to their DSO so that the school can confirm that the student is participating in an established curriculum where practical training is integral, make a determination that the training is directly related to the studentâs major area of study, and update the studentâs SEVIS record to ensure that DHS can conduct proper oversight as required under federal law.Must all CPT be conducted by sponsoring employers that have established cooperative agreements with the school?Yes. Schools should only enter into cooperative agreements with legitimate, bona fide employers who are able to provide a quality practical training experience to students. CPT students should have access to practical training managed by an employer who has entered into a cooperative agreement with a school where it is agreed the employer will sponsor the schoolâs students for specific training such as an alternative work/study, internship, cooperative education or any other type of required internship or practicum that is specific to the studentâs major area of study. Students are not expected to obtain EADs for this training which is an integral and required part of the curriculum.Immigration attorney Emily Neumann said this is not how CPT is used by universities. "When an agency needs a second, three-page broadcast just 12 days later to explain what the first one meant, that tells you the first one raised some serious questions," Neumann wrote.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Celebridades y amigos del espectáculo dan el último adiós a Dolly Parton
articles.summary: Dolly Parton falleció este martes a los 80 años, y las celebridades le dan el último adiós a través de fotos, recuerdos y bellas palabras para honrar su lega...
articles.body:
El mundo de la música y el espectáculo se viste de luto para despedir a Dolly Parton, fallecida a los 80 años. Este martes, su sobrino, Bryan Seaver , confirmó el lamentable suceso a través de un video que pronto tocó corazones al rededor del mundo. Ante la sorpresiva noticia, amigos y conocidos de Dolly han dedicado algunas palabras para honrar su memoria.

"Gracias, Dolly. Por todo", escribió la actriz junto a una foto de la cantante. en un mensaje más extenso, anotó: "Dicen que no debes conocer a tus héroes. Se equivocaban con ella. Su valentía al reconocer que era más de lo que otros creían —y al comprender que necesitaba romper con el pasado para emprender nuevos proyectos y explorar nuevas posibilidades— la llevó a escribir *I Will Always Love You*; fue su manera de expresar gratitud y afecto, sin dejar de avanzar. Es un gran ejemplo para todos nosotros".

El empresario dedicó unas palabras en memoria a su amiga: "Dolly pasó toda su vida mostrándonos lo que significa liderar con amor. Lauren y yo estamos profundamente agradecidos de haberla conocido. Ella elevaba el ánimo de todos con su música, su generosidad y su alegría. Enviamos nuestras más sinceras condolencias a su familia y a todas las personas a quienes llegó su influencia".

Tal como Jeff, Lauren se tomó un momento para destacar la grandeza de Parton: "Dolly se ha ido y tengo el corazón destrozado. Crecí escuchando su música. Me sabía todas las canciones de memoria. Y aún me las sé. Ella estuvo presente en los mejores días de mi vida y en los peores, aunque ni siquiera lo supiera. Eso es lo que hizo por millones de nosotros".

Y continuó: "Luego llegué a conocerla y, de alguna manera, resultó ser más que una leyenda. Ella fue quien dio sentido a nuestro premio al Coraje y la Civilidad, y no al revés. Decía que siempre había intentado invertir su dinero allí donde estaba su corazón. Su corazón estaba con los niños. Siempre lo estuvo. Libros gratuitos enviados por correo a niños que no tenían ninguno —mes tras mes, durante treinta años— porque su padre nunca aprendió a leer. Las canciones seguirán sonando. Todos nos sabemos la letra. Gracias, Dolly".

La hija de Ozzy Osbourne también expresó su dolor a través de palabras: "Dolly, gracias por abrir camino. No solo para las mujeres en la música, sino para que las mujeres de todas partes sean ellas mismas sin complejos. Nos demostraste que podíamos ser ambiciosas y amables, fuertes y sensibles, valientes y auténticas".

Y añadió: "Uno de los mayores honores de mi vida fue tener la oportunidad de trabajar contigo. Tu legado trasciende la música. A través de tu filantropía, tu generosidad y tu compromiso con la alfabetización y la educación, has cambiado innumerables vidas y has hecho del mundo un lugar mejor. Utilizaste tu éxito para impulsar a los demás, demostrando que la verdadera grandeza no se mide solo por lo que logramos, sino por lo que damos". Kelly concluyó: "Nunca habrá otra Dolly Parton. Gracias por la música, las risas, el amor y por dejar este mundo más luminoso, más amable y mejor de como lo encontraste".

La diseñadora escribió: "El mundo ha perdido a una de las almas más bondadosas y generosas, a la mejor narradora de historias y a una verdadera leyenda de la música. Tantas vidas mejoraron gracias a ti. Gracias, Dolly, por todo".

La también cantante anotó: "Bueno, acabo de recibir la noticia de que mi amiga Dolly ha partido hacia un plano superior y maravilloso. Dolly, gracias por todas las cosas maravillosas que hiciste por nosotros aquí en la tierra. Tu amor, tu música y todo lo que entregaste con tu inmenso corazón". Y continuó: "Nunca, jamás, habrá otra como tú. Recordaremos y atesoraremos cada recuerdo y cada nota que tocaste y cantaste. Gracias, Señor, por Dolly. Lo pasará de maravilla en el cielo cantando todas sus canciones favoritas con su familia y amigos que se adelantaron en el camino. Nunca olvidaré la primera vez que te conocí ni nuestra última conversación; la guardo con amor en mi corazón. Siempre te amaré, Reba".

El presidente Trump se pronunció sobre la muerte de Dolly y expresó: "En su honor, ordeno que se ice a media asta la bandera estadounidense en todo el país durante una semana, a partir de esta noche a las 6:00 p. m. ¡Descansa en paz, Dolly! El mundo te quiere".

La actriz de Sex And the City se unió a las condolencias: "Nunca conocí a @dollyparton, pero madre mía, cuánto la quería. No creo que hiciera falta conocerla para quererla. Una de las más grandes que ha dado este país. Una leyenda. De verdad. Para siempre. Y siempre defendiendo a quienes ella sabía —y entendía— que necesitaban una defensora. Qué gran pérdida. Pero qué suerte, qué fortuna la nuestra por los regalos infinitos que compartió. Con el mundo. Buen viaje y descansa en paz. Se te echará muchísimo de menos.

La presentadora de TV no podía creer la lamentabe pérdida de la cantante: "Publiqué esto ayer. No puedo creer las noticias de hoy. Qué leyenda hemos perdido. Envío todo mi cariño a quienes la querían. Dolly Parton me habló de la persona real en la que se inspiró para su imagen".

El productor y esposo de Thalía, se conmovió al enterarse de la lamentable noticia: "Con el corazón roto 💔 por la noticia del fallecimiento de DOLLY... fue la primera artista de música country con la que tuve el privilegio de trabajar en SONY MUSIC... llevando su amor, su LUZ y su hermosa música y composiciones a todo el mundo... y brindando tanta alegría a quienes trabajaban con ella... Fue más que icónica y legendaria. ¡¡¡ERA LA ESENCIA Y EL ALMA, UNA PIEZA CENTRAL INDELEBLE Y ETERNA DE LA MÚSICA COUNTRY!!!Descansa en paz para siempre, dulce DOLLY 🙏🏼🙏🏼💔".

Uno de mis recuerdos más entrañables junto a @dollyparton: divertirme a lo grande luciendo vestidos de Bob Mackie en su programa 'Dolly'. Esta chica de las Montañas Humeantes de Tennessee soñó con una vida y luego vivió una existencia más grandiosa de lo que jamás hubiera imaginado, entregándose a los demás con enorme generosidad, tanto de formas que vimos como de otras que no. No hay nadie como ella. Ella trajo luz al mundo, y todos somos mejores gracias a que estuvo aquí. Que Dios te bendiga, Dolly; te has ganado tus alas 🪽".

En medio de los mensajes, resaltó el de Sheryl Crow: "Hay un vacío en el universo. Nunca hubo ni habrá nadie como Dolly. No la conocía bien, pero la quería como a una más de la familia... todos la queríamos. Era una narradora increíble, tanto en la música como en la vida real".

La cantante anotó: "Dolly Parton tenía una manera de hacer que todos se sintieran especiales, vistos y bienvenidos, como si fueran viejos amigos. Extrañaré su corazón y su voz, tal como estoy seguro de que lo harán millones de personas. Qué regalo y talento tan increíbles representaba —y sigue representando—, gracias al maravilloso legado artístico que nos ha dejado a todos".

articles.title: Iran, Oman discuss temporary shipping lane through Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary: Omani FM hopes the two countries will ‘soon announce’ a joint temporary transit corridor through the Strait of Hormuz.
articles.body:
Iran and Oman's top diplomats have discussed a proposed framework for a temporary transit corridor through the Strait of Hormuz and a mine-clearing project in the key waterway, which they both border.

Oman's Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi arrived in Tehran on Tuesday for talks with his Iranian counterpart, Abbas Araghchi, to discuss future plans for the strait.

The two "discussed a phased framework that could provide a practical and implementable basis for moving forward", they said in a joint statement shared by Oman.

The strait became a flashpoint early in the Middle East war, and the two countries have recently sought to hammer out a plan to regulate transit through it, as laid out in a June US-Iran memorandum of understanding aimed at ending the war.

"The proposed framework includes the establishment of a temporary joint navigation corridor through the Strait of Hormuz and an agreement to implement a joint project to clear the Strait of mines," the statement said.

"Technical negotiations between the two sides will also continue with the aim of reaching an agreement on a permanent navigation corridor and future arrangements for managing the Strait, alongside establishing a mechanism for exchanging information, managing navigation traffic, and providing related navigational and security services," it added.

Albusaidi said in a post on X after the meeting that he hoped the countries would "soon announce" the temporary corridor in the strait.

"Future management of the strait and a permanent solution will follow in due course," he said.

During their meeting, the two ministers also stressed the importance of reaching arrangements that respect the sovereignty of their respective countries, according to the joint statement.

The diplomats "affirmed the importance of holding joint discussions with the Gulf littoral [coastal] states" to ensure that any agreement reached adheres to international law and respects the sovereignty of neighbouring countries.

The statement came after US President Donald Trump said on his social platform Truth Social that "all mines have been removed and/or detonated from within the International Waters of the Strait of Hormuz", citing the US navy.

"Iran has been notified that any ship or boat placing new mines will be immediately and systematically destroyed," Trump added.

War broke out after the US and Israel attacked Iran on February 28, with Tehran quickly blockading the Strait of Hormuz and Washington imposing a naval counter-blockade on Iranian ports.

Traffic remains largely paralysed, disrupting global oil markets in a crucial waterway that normally carries around one-fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas exports.

Iran and Oman, both coastal nations on the strait, have for weeks been discussing the future of navigation through the waterway, with Tehran saying the geographical coordinates of a route envisaged by the two countries "have been agreed upon".

Iranian officials, however, have insisted that the strait will not fully reopen until the US meets Tehran's demands, including lifting its naval blockade, dropping oil sanctions and unfreezing its assets abroad.
